column2: As many as were created attend them; the truth, as it was, is firm for you; they are Brahmins'.
Others who were weak were stationed in the work of protection; those on earth destroyed what was bought.
They call them Vaishyas, those who bring about livelihood by tilling; and those who serve and flow, devoted to attendance,
lacking brilliance and of little valour, he called Shudras. The lord Brahma ordained their actions and duties.
When the arrangement of the four varnas was made by him, those people through delusion again did not keep that dharma.
Living by the dharmas of varnas, they obstructed one another. Brahma, understanding all that as it was, the lord,
assigned to Kshatriyas strength, punishment, war and its livelihood; to Brahmins sacrificing, teaching, giving and accepting gifts.
Of them the lord thus assigned these works; he gave cattle-keeping, trade and agriculture to the Vaishyas.
And he ordained for the Shudras the livelihood of craftsmen; and common actions for Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas.
Sacrifice, study and giving are common to the others; having given them mutually a livelihood by action,
he again established their places in the other worlds at the head: the Prajapati's place is remembered for the twice-born who perform rites;
Indra's place for Kshatriyas who do not flee in battles; the Maruts' place for Vaishyas who live by their own work;
the Gandharva place for the Shudra classes who remain in service. These are the places of the varnas, of the good with proper conduct.
When the arrangement of the four varnas was well made, the varnas stood each in its own from fear of punishment. Then, the varnas being established, he established the ashramas:
householder, celibate student, forest-dweller and ascetic. The lord established these four ashramas as before.
Those who are of the works of varnas, the fourfold among them, having done their works and made their abode, enjoy by the ashrama.
Brahma established those ashramas for the wandering; then Brahma declared their dharmas.
Their departures, restraints and observances: the householder's ashrama, formerly made of the four varnas, stands.
And the source of livelihood of the three ashramas — I shall tell in order, with vows and observances.
Wife, fires, guests, sacrifices, shraddha rites and offspring: this is in brief the compendium of the householder's dharma.
Staff, girdle, sleeping on the ground and deer-skin, service to the teacher, alms: these are for the student seeking learning.
Bark, leaves and skins, forest roots, fruits and herbs; bathing at both twilights and fire-offering for forest-dwellers.
Alms when the pestle is idle, non-stealing and purity, heedfulness, chastity, compassion toward beings and forbearance,
hearing, service to the teacher, and truth as the tenth are remembered; this dharma of ten marks was declared by the Self-born.
For the mendicant there are five vows and the vows of alms and Veda; he told their places as established.
Eighty-eight thousand sages of upward seed: their place is remembered, the same as that of those living with teachers.
The place of the Seven Sages is remembered as that of forest-dwellers; the Prajapati place for householders, Brahma's abode for renunciants.
The place of yogis is unmade; without conquering it is not found. The places of the ashrama-dwellers stand in Brahma's station.
Four paths of the gods were made, and four paths of the ancestors are remembered.
By the world-system of Brahma, in the first manvantara long ago, the paths of the gods have the Sun remembered as their door, and likewise the moon is called the door of the paths of the ancestors.
Thus when the division of varnas and ashramas was made, then when the creatures did not increase, being kept by the dharma of varnas,
then he created another mental progeny of his own in the middle of Treta, equal to himself, from his own bodies.
In that first Treta yuga, when the middle had come in order, he then began to create another mental progeny.
Then the lord created creatures pervaded by sattva and rajas, who were accomplishers of dharma, wealth, desire, liberation and livelihood —
gods, ancestors, sages and Manus, by whom these creatures were increased by dharma suited to the yuga.
When that group of the Self-born's creation had come, Brahma reflected on his mental creatures of various powers,
those mentioned to you by me before, who had taken refuge in the host of people; in the past kalpa, in earlier cities, creatures such as gods were here.
As he meditated, they presented themselves for coming into being, in order of manvantaras, the youngest by the first.
They were famed by these families, by whom they were formerly brought into being here, then joined with undiminished roots of good and bad.
By the fault of the fruit of that action, afflictions were born: among gods, Asuras, ancestors, Yakshas, Gandharvas, humans,
Rakshasas, Pishachas, animals, birds, reptiles, trees, hell-beings, insects and the like, all were present. For the livelihood of creatures the knower of himself made (provisions).
With her he sports; therefore she is called Rati. That first union occurred at the beginning of the kalpa.
Brahma created Viraj; he became the Purusha Virat. Samrat, with Shatarupa, was Vairaja, remembered as Manu.
That Vairaja Purusha Manu created the creation of creatures; from the Vairaja Purusha, Shatarupa bore two heroes.
Priyavrata and Uttanapada, the best of fathers of sons; and two very fortunate daughters from whom these creatures are born,
named Devi and Akuti, and Prasuti, auspicious ones. The lord gave Prasuti, Svayambhuva's, to Daksha,
and gave Akuti to the Prajapati Ruchi. On Akuti was born a pair, auspicious, of the mind-born Ruchi:
Yajna and Dakshina, they became twins. Of Yajna and Dakshina twelve sons were born,
famed as the Yamas, gods of the Svayambhuva (manvantara) and others; because they were sons of Yajna, they are remembered as Yamas.
The Ajitas and the Shukras are remembered as two groups of Brahma; the Yamas who went before, whose names are of the dwellers in heaven.
On Prasuti, Svayambhuva's daughter, mothers of the world, Daksha the lord begot twenty-four daughters.
All of them fortunate, all lotus-eyed, all wives of yoga, all mothers of yoga,
all Brahman-speakers, all mothers of the universe: Shraddha, Lakshmi, Dhriti, Tushti, Pushti, Medha, Kriya,
Buddhi, Lajja, Vasu, Shanti, Siddhi, Kirti — thirteen; Dharma, the lord, took the daughters of Daksha as wives.
These doors were ordained for him by the Self-born; the eleven lovely-eyed ones who remained, the younger:
Sati, Khyati, Sambhuti, Smriti, Priti, Kshama, Sannati, Anasuya, Urja, Svaha and Svadha.
They were then accepted by other great sages: Rudra, Bhrigu, Marichi, Angiras, Pulaha, Kratu,
Pulastya, Atri, Vasishtha, the ancestors and Agni. He gave Sati to Bhava, and Khyati to Bhrigu;
Sambhuti to Marichi, Smriti to Angiras, Priti to Pulastya and Kshama to Pulaha,
Santati to Kratu, Anasuya to Atri, Urja to Vasishtha, Svaha to Agni,
and Svadha to the ancestors; hear from me their offspring. All these fortunate ones followed the progeny and stand,
in all manvantaras until the dissolution of beings. Shraddha bore Kama, then Darpa; Lakshmi's son is remembered.
Dhriti's son was Niyama, Tushti's is called Santosha, Pushti's son Labha, and Medha's son was Shruta.
Of Kriya two sons are told: Dama and Shama. Buddhi's son was Bodha, and Apramada; these two.
Lajja's son was Vinaya, Vasu's son Vyavasaya, Shanti's son Kshema, and Siddhi bore Sukha.
Kirti's son was Yasha: these are the sons of Dharma. Kama's son Harsha was born of the goddess Siddhi.
Thus this sattvic creation of Dharma has pleasant results. From Adharma were born Himsa, and Nikriti and Anrita.
From Nikriti and Anrita were born Bhaya and Naraka; Maya and Vedana, the pairs of these two.
From Maya was born Mrityu, taker of beings; from Vedana was born Duhkha, from Raurava.
From Mrityu were born Vyadhi, Jara, Shoka, Krodha and Asuya. These are remembered as with sorrow last, all marked by adharma.
They have wives or sons; all are remembered as without end. Thus this tamasic creation was born, regulator of dharma.
Commanded by Brahma, "Create creatures," the dark-red one (Rudra), reflecting on Sati his wife, made beings from himself.
Neither more nor less than him, those mental beings equal to himself, he created a thousand thousands, hide-clad.
All equal to himself in form, brilliance, strength and learning: tawny, with quivers, matted-haired, dark-red,
tuftless and hairless, eye-destroying, skull-bearing, great-formed and deformed, universal-formed and having forms,
with chariots, armour, bows, and retinues, with thousands and hundreds of arms, going in heaven, earth and atmosphere,
with thick heads, eight tusks, two tongues, three eyes, eaters of food and flesh, drinkers of ghee and soma,
with great organs and fierce bodies, dark-necked, fiercely wrathful, with quivers and armour, bow-bearers, with swords and shields,
seated, running, yawning, presiding, studying, muttering, yoking, meditating,
blazing, raining, shining, fumigated, awakened and most awakened, possessed of Brahman, seeing Brahman,
blue-necked, thousand-eyed, all practising patience, invisible to all beings, great yogis, of great vigour,
weeping and running; thousands thus joined. Creating these unwearied best of gods, Rudra,
Brahma, seeing them, said to him: "Do not create such creatures. Creatures equal to yourself are not to be created, nor greater.
Create others, may you be well, creatures joined with death; creatures free of death do not undertake actions."
Thus addressed, he said, "I shall not create creatures endowed with death and old age, may you be well; I stand firm; you create, lord.
These whom I created, deformed, dark-red, thousand thousands have issued from my self.
These will be gods, named Rudras, greatly mighty, famed on earth and in the atmosphere as Rudranis.
They are taught in the Shatarudriya, and will here be worthy of sacrifice; all will be sharers of sacrifice with the hosts of gods.
The gods who will be here in the manvantaras, born of metres, with them being worshipped they will stay here until the yuga's end."
Thus addressed by Mahadeva, the lord Brahma, seen by the Prajapati, replied to the terrible one:
So be it, may you be well, as you have said, lord. Permitted by Brahma, then all came to be.
From then on that god did not beget creatures, but stood with upward seed, as Sthanu, until the dissolution of beings.
Because he said "I stand," therefore the wise remember him as Sthanu. Knowledge, austerity, truth, lordship and dharma,
dispassion and self-realisation: all of these are in Shankara. All the gods and sages gathered with the Asuras
the god surpasses by brilliance, therefore he is remembered as Mahadeva; he surpasses the gods by lordship and the great Asuras by strength,
all sages by knowledge and all beings by yoga. Thus Mahadeva, bowed to by all gods, having created the progeny of the sky, ceased from creation.
The fourth, of the fourth (name), is your body Vayu. When so said, what in his body was called the fivefold life-breath
entered that wind of his, Ishana's body, the wind. Therefore one should not revile the wind, the Lord, as it blows.
Those who deal with him in sacrifices and serve him — the god Maheshana does not harm one so joined.
Then Brahma again said to the god, the lord, "The fifth name I declared, Pashupati,
this is the fifth body: let Agni be yours by name." When so said, the heat in his body called warmth
then entered Agni; hence he is Pashupati, because Agni was the animal and protects animals.
Therefore Pashupati's body is called Agni; hence one should not burn the impure nor warm the feet at it,
nor put it below, nor step over it; Pashupati, the god, does not harm one so joined.
Then Brahma again said to the white-tawny god, "The sixth name I spoke for you is Bhima, lord.
Let space be the body of that name, the sixth." When so said, the hollow in his body
entered space then; that is the body of Bhima. Since the god is remembered in space, therefore he is never covered:
one should not urinate or defecate, eat or drink, have intercourse or throw leavings (toward it).
The god does not harm one who acts so toward Bhima. Then Brahma again said to the god with strength, the lord:
The seventh name I declared, Ugra, lord: the body of that name for you is the initiated twice-born.
When so said, the consciousness in his body entered the initiated Brahmin, the soma-sacrificer.
For as long, Brahmins, Ugra is remembered as the god initiated; therefore one should not revile him nor speak obscenity of him.
Those who revile him take away his sin; the god Ugra does not harm Brahmins so joined.
Then Brahma again said to the god, bright as the sun: "The eighth name declared by me is Mahadeva.
The body of the eighth name for you is the moon." When so said, what was the lord's resolving mind
entered the moon; therefore Mahadeva appears as the moon. On the new moon the twice-born should not cut trees, shrubs or herbs;
Mahadeva is remembered as Soma, his self is the host of herbs. One who always acts so at each parva
is not killed by Mahadeva, who knows the lord so. By day the Sun guards creatures, by night the moon;
the sun and moon meet in one night, on the night of the new moon; on that night one should be always joined (in devotion).
All this is pervaded by Rudra, by bodies and names. This sun, roaming alone, is called Rudra;
by the light of the sun creatures see with the eye. Rudra, standing liberated, drinks water with his rays;
it is eaten and drunk by desire for food and drink. That body born of water increases in bodies;
by which he supports all creatures with firm brilliance. The earthly one is his body, the virtuous one that bears creatures.
That which stays in bodies of beings by the functions of life-breath
is Ishani, of the nature of wind, life-breath in living beings here; it digests what is drunk and eaten in beings' bellies here.
His Pashupata body is called the digesting Agni. The hollow spaces within bodies
for the movement of wind are called the terrible body. The state of the initiated Brahman-speakers in the Vaitana (ritual)
is the fierce-natured body; hence the initiated is remembered as Ugra. The resolving mind of his that is established in creatures here
is his mental body, the moon, stationed in beings. Newer and newer, born again and again,
he is drunk in time by the wise with the ancestors. Mahadeva, immortal-souled, is remembered as the moon, made of water.
His first body by name, Raudri, is declared; his wife Suvarchala, and her son Shanaishchara.
Bhava's second body by name is remembered as Water; her wife Dhatri is remembered, and son Ushana.
Sharva's third name, Earth, is the body; her wife is Vikeshi and her son Angaraka.
Ishana's fourth name, Wind, is the body; her wife is called Shiva and her son Manojava,
and two sons of Anila, Avijnatagati. By the name Pashupati the body is Agni, say the Brahmins;
her wife is Svaha, and her son Skanda. The sixth name, Bhima, body, is called space;
the directions are remembered as his wives, and Svarga as his son. The seventh, Ugra, body is the initiated Brahmin;
Diksha is his wife, and Santana his son. The eighth name Mahas, body, is remembered as the moon;
his wife is Rohini and his son Budha. Thus these his bodies are told together with their names.
In these he is to be bowed to and honoured in each name-body: in the sun, in the earth, in wind, in fire, in space, in the initiated,
in devotees and in the moon, with devotion, by the names. One who knows that god thus with bodies and names
with offspring attains union with Ishvara Bhava. Thus this secret has been told to you by me, the fame of this Bhima.
May there be well-being for our two-footed, Brahmins, and for our four-footed. This has now been told with the names of the bodies of the god Mahadeva; hear of Bhrigu, descendants.
Yajurdhama, and the wise Stambakashyapa; the two sons, founders of gotras, were born, resolved in renunciation.
Smriti was the wife of Angiras; she bore children of her own: a son and four holy daughters, famed in the world:
Sinivali, Kuhu, Raka and Anumati; and likewise Bharata-Agni and Kirtiman, those two.
Sadvati bore Agni's son Parjanya; Hiranyaroma Parjanya was born of Marichi's daughter.
Staying until the dissolution of beings, he is remembered as a world-guardian; at Kirtiman's sacrifice also, Dhenuka and Vitakalmasha,
Charishnu and Dhritiman, both the best of the Angirases; their sons and grandsons have passed away by thousands.
Anasuya bore five faultless Atreyas, and a daughter named Shruti, the mother of Shankhapada.
